answer_1.quote: We propose a grey-box framework that generates high quality textual adversarial examples while simultaneously trains an improved sentiment classifier for adversarial defending.

answer_2.quote: In addition to measuring how well the adversarial examples fool the sentiment classifier, we also use a number of automatic metrics to assess other aspects of adversarial examples, following : Attacking performance. We use the standard classification accuracy (ACC) of the target classifier (C) to measure the attacking performance of adversarial examples. Lower accuracy means better attacking performance. Similarity. To assess the textual and semantic similarity between the original and corresponding adversarial examples, we compute BLEU  and USE . 8 For both metrics, higher scores represent better performance. Fluency. To measure the readability of generated adversarial examples, we use the acceptability score (ACPT) proposed by Lau et al. ( ), which is based on normalised sentence probabilities produced by XLNet . Higher scores indicate better fluency.

answer_4.quote: To validate that these metrics work, we conduct a crowdsourcing experiment on Appen.
answer_4.guideline: We ask crowdworkers the following questions: 1. Is snippet B a good paraphrase of snippet A? Yes Somewhat yes No 2. How natural does the text read? Very unnatural Somewhat natural Natural 3. What is the sentiment of the text? Positive Negative Cannot tell
